findings.detail: The plan and M7.26 acceptance say 'a dangling binding shows a problem and Fix frees the endpoint' as an E2E. e2e/validation.fix-broken-ref.spec.ts drives the stacked-elements warning (Select, Offset the top one) and never a dangling binding or a freed end. The m7-complete leg is labelled 'the validation panel lists a dangling binding and fixes it' and only runs that spec, so it can go green with the label false. The reachability argument (M7.26 F1: no UI path makes a dangling binding) is sound for the E2E, but then the leg label and the acceptance are wrong and the real proof (problems-tab.browser.test 'FR-EDT-021: a binding to a missing element is listed and Free the end ...', problems.test.ts) is not pinned by the gate.

findings.detail: FR-EDT-021 lists broken references, missing assets, overlap warnings and contrast warnings. The Problems tab has validate() diagnostics and one lint approximation: elements with an identical box. Contrast is absent; 'overlap' is exact stacking only; the plan names 'lintRules'. M7.26 F2 argues this to M14 (lintRules registry, FR-AI-005), but no row exists: M14.md row 10 builds the registry and has no item for the editor panel to read it, and the roadmap Deferred table has no line. An argued line is not a hand-off; the requirement is M7's by the traceability matrix and nothing receives the rest.

findings.detail: check-budget --record times 'precommit.mjs --staged' on whatever is staged at that moment. With the scope reductions of M7.32-M7.35 (docs, e2e, gate scripts, sources run a fraction; coverage and packaging left to CI) an empty or small stage is a trivially fast run: stagedMs fell from 112399 to 30655 and quickMs from 19519 to 5878 without any code change in the ladder between the two numbers' commits (the record's commit field is 9e6bbc9, before M7.32). PRECOMMIT_BUDGET_MS (120 s) therefore no longer constrains the worst real staged commit, which is a manifest or script change that still runs everything. coldSetupMs rose 183000 to 297000 (limit 600000) and is a real CI number, which is fine.
findings.failure_scenario: A commit staging a shared helper or a tsconfig runs the full ladder at 200 s again and the green budget leg never notices.

findings.detail: Checked for weakening: --all (CI's pnpm verify, ci.yml line 47) still runs every harness file, the coverage run, publint and attw, so nothing is dropped; unknown paths fall back to every file (null), and the tests pin that mixing one unknown path runs everything. Remaining risk is design, not a defect: a staged doc runs the files that name its literal path (naming() greps file text), so a harness test that reads docs by directory glob or by a built path is not found and misses a staged edit until CI. harnessFor also treats any docs/*.md as docs, e.g. docs/requirements edits, which docs-consistency and trace cover. No gate was loosened and no threshold changed. Argue.
findings.failure_scenario: A doc edit breaks a harness test that builds its path at run time; the commit is green and CI is red.

findings.detail: optionGlyph maps both 'center' and 'width' to the same arrow and falls back to the first letter, so icons are ambiguous in a field whose options collide; names stay in aria-label and title, so it is not an accessibility defect. The arrow-step, rejected-entry and gesture-ref changes are correct and each has a titled test; PaintField no longer shows gradient/image as 'none' and does not rewrite them on blur.

1) inspector.browser 'arrow keys step a number': a mutant making stepped() ignore shift (always 1) fails at 91; a mutant dropping seal() fails the one-undo-step assertion. Constrains. 2) problems.test 'dangling binding': a mutant that drops the elementId path check (fix for any FLX_REF_MISSING) still passes only if the fix args stay equal, so the test pins args exactly; a mutant that frees 'source' instead of 'target' fails. Constrains. 3) ladder-scope 'a doc, an e2e spec...': a mutant returning E2E_HARNESS for every e2e/ path is the intended behaviour; a mutant adding 'coverage' back to DOCS_HARNESS passes the equality check only if only() is rebuilt from the same constant (it is: the assertions compare against the exported arrays, so the test is partly circular for DOCS_HARNESS, E2E_HARNESS and GATE_SCRIPT_HARNESS). Weak: add literal expected names for at least the docs case.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone adds 'coverage' to DOCS_HARNESS; the test follows the constant and stays green.
